aldemar.headline: Iran and Oman draw a corridor through the minefield — and Nvidia answers the AI question after the bell
aldemar.standfirst: Wednesday produced the two things this market has been waiting three weeks for. Tehran and Muscat put a concrete mechanism on the table — a temporary joint maritime corridor plus mine clearance, with a permanent route to be negotiated inside 30 to 60 days — and crude fell a third straight session, WTI −2.6% to 80.21 and Brent under $86. Then Nvidia reported $96.2bn of revenue, up 106%, guided Q3 to $108bn and Jensen Huang declared "AI has reached its inflection point"; the stock went from −1.3% to +5% after hours. The tape itself closed flat ahead of it. PCE came in sticky — core 3.3%, unchanged.

positions.title: 1 signal on INTC — read before the open (BAC quiet)

items.html: INTC — Nvidia's blowout is the sector verdict Aldemar's thesis was waiting on — INTC +0.87% to 88.24 after an 85.63 low. The print answers the question Monday's brief said would decide this position: $96.2bn revenue (+106%), data centre $89.0bn (+117%), and a Q3 guide of $108bn against a $57bn year-ago base. Huang's line — "its tokens are productive and profitable" — attacks the exact doubt that has been de-rating the whole complex since Alphabet's bond deal. If the AI build-out is demand-validated rather than debt-financed, the CPU-inference case that got Aldemar into this at 105.81 gets its footing back. Wednesday's own action already hinted: a 85.63 low bought back to close near the 88.28 high, the first genuine reversal bar of the drawdown. He is −16.6% on entry at −0.71R with the 81.10 stop 8.1% below. Today's open is where the sector read-across gets priced — and $95 remains the level the new holders paid.

BAC — BAC −0.32% to 62.23, holding the 62 shelf for a third session as core PCE stays stuck at 3.3%. No company news; the position is simply sitting on its level with a 61.93 low that respected it again. The macro underneath is quietly supportive rather than not: core PCE unchanged at 3.3% year-on-year keeps the Fed restrictive, which is the condition the steepener needs — though the two wires read it differently, one calling it room to hold and the other reinforced restriction. Gabriel −3.34% on entry at −0.54R, stop 60.39 3.0% below; Aldemar −3.01% at −0.43R, stop 59.65 4.1% below. Confirmation of the thesis is not the same as a change to it, so this stays filed as noise.

positions.note: Signal changes the thesis, the levels or the size — earnings, a regulator with teeth, M&A, a ruling with a revenue line attached. Everything else is filed as noise on purpose; a real signal survives skepticism.

themes.right: interim corridor proposed · mine clearance · 30–60 day permanent route
themes.title: The first actual mechanism: a joint corridor, swept of mines, with a deadline attached

items.html: Iran and Oman negotiate an interim framework — a temporary joint maritime corridor plus a mine-clearance project, with a permanent route targeted in 30 to 60 days. This is categorically different from last week's atmospherics. Deputy Foreign Minister Gharibabadi described technical talks covering corridor administration, information exchange and maritime security services — the plumbing of an actual reopening rather than a statement about wanting one. The strait has been largely closed since March.

Tehran insists the Hormuz track is independent of US negotiations; Trump says the Navy is mine-clearing. Iran is deliberately separating the waterway from the broader war so one can move without the other — and conditions any return to US talks on Washington honouring the June deal. The analyst read is blunt: the wildcard is whether the administration backs a framework it did not broker.

WTI −2.6% to 80.21, Brent under $86 — a third straight decline and roughly 8% off last Thursday's high. The premium keeps draining as the reopening path becomes specific. At 80 rather than 87 the arithmetic that has been propping the inflation gate open starts to reverse, and energy stops being the reason the regime call survives.

themes.note: The transmission is oil → inflation → the regime call, and for the first time the friendly direction has a mechanism and a clock rather than a mood. But Wednesday also showed the limit of that: core PCE came in unchanged at 3.3%, which says the inflation already in the system is not an energy artefact and will not fall just because crude does. So the regime survives this week regardless — what changes is the marginal risk. Watch for a start date on the technical talks; if the corridor gets scheduled, crude has further to give, and the war stops being the first line of this brief.

world.title: A flat session that was entirely a waiting room — and the answer arrived at 4:20

items.html: Nvidia: revenue $96.2bn (+106%), EPS $2.22 (+111%), data centre $89.0bn (+117%), Q3 guided to $108bn ±2%; the stock swung from −1.3% to +5% after hours. Gross margin expanded to 75% and the AWS partnership widened. This is the demand-side rebuttal to the financing audit that has run the tape all month: the question was whether the datacentre build-out earns anything, and the bellwether answered with an 89% growth guide. It had fallen eight straight sessions into the print, so positioning was short into a beat.

PCE: headline +0.2% m/m and 3.7% y/y, core 3.3% — unchanged from June. Sticky rather than hot. Core holding at 3.3% while crude falls 8% is the important combination: it separates the inflation problem from the war, and it keeps the Fed's hands tied in both directions. The read splits the desks — more time to hold, or reinforced restriction — which is exactly why Jackson Hole matters this week.

S&P −0.02%, Nasdaq marginally green, Dow −0.21%, Russell +0.50%; Abercrombie +30.9% on a beat, Intuit −9.2% on guidance. An index that did nothing over a session of violent single-name dispersion. Note the pattern repeating: Intuit beat and was sold for its outlook, Abercrombie beat and was bought — guidance, not results, is what the tape is trading, and that is the same lens Nvidia's $108bn guide just passed through.

Dealer gamma stays modestly positive with spot still pinned near the flip at 7,670. A third session balanced on the boundary, which is why the index kept closing flat while individual names moved 10% and 30%. That balance breaks today: an after-hours 5% move in the market's largest name is exactly the kind of gap that resolves a tape sitting on its flip.

weekly.headline: Gold's best week of the year against the book's hardest — and the war became the weather
weekly.standfirst: The week opened with a dead deadline and closed with a dead framework: the memorandum expired Monday, missiles landed off the UAE Tuesday, China-linked supertankers turned around Thursday, and by Friday Washington was asking a refusing Beijing to help sanction Tehran. Equities absorbed it slowly — the S&P lost 1.43%, chips roughly 10% as the AI-financing audit claimed Intel's $20B raise — while gold ran 6.6% to three records and crude added 5.4%. The book paid its first real tuition: Gabriel's INTC stopped out at exactly −1R on Tuesday, both BAC positions broke their 62 line after Walmart repriced the consumer, and GOOG quietly held the whole time. The market leaves the week in negative gamma for the first time all month.

WARThe memorandum expired Monday and nothing replaced it — by Friday the war was structural. Missiles off the UAE, a projectile-struck ship, supertankers turning back, transits −19.5%, US pump prices +$1 y/y. The market stopped trading war headlines and started pricing a war baseline: Brent +5% on the week with acceleration, not spikes.CBS · Al Jazeera · Trading Economics · 17–21 Aug
TECHThe AI-financing audit claimed its biggest name: Intel's $20B raise at $95 → a 90.07 Friday close, chips −10% on the week. Dilution priced at a discount, marked below the offer within two sessions, and the whole complex re-rated with it. Add Wednesday's tepid OpenAI numbers and the audit now questions both how the build-out is funded and what it earns. Nvidia next week is the verdict.TradingKey · Trading Economics · 18–21 Aug
CONSUMERWalmart's guidance cut turned a data wobble into a confirmed slowdown — BAC broke its 62 line on the news. Retail sales −0.6%, sentiment 51, then the biggest retailer in the country blinked (−8.8% Thursday, −10% on the week). For a bank long the US consumer's balance sheet, the credit side of the thesis is now live risk, with the steepener side still intact against it.Eurasia Business News · Seeking Alpha · 14–20 Aug
METALSGold +6.6% — three records in five sessions, accelerating into strength. War premium, debt concerns, and a Treasury forced to buy its own long bonds: the debasement trade graduated from hedge to position. It was the single most profitable trade on the board this week, and nobody had to pick a stock to have it.Yahoo Finance · TradingKey · 17–21 Aug
NOISEFiled and ignored: target trims following Intel's share count, chart-pattern notes on BAC, a Pixel launch, an Alphabet retrospective. A full week of commentary that described moves after they happened. None of it changed a thesis, a level, or a size.various · 17–21 Aug

The discipline ledger matters as much as the P&L this week: Gabriel's INTC exit filled at exactly the planned 95.52 — a clean −1.00R, taken on schedule, with no slippage on a −6.6% day. That is the system doing precisely what it was built to do. The open book ends the week: Gabriel +0.79R on GOOG against −0.67R on BAC; Aldemar −0.55R on BAC and −0.64R on INTC, both inside their planned risk with stops standing.

sections.html:
From deadline to baseline: the week the war stopped being an event

TALKSMonday: the 60-day memorandum expires; Trump demands surrender and threatens Oman, the mediator. The only structure containing the conflict lapsed with neither side asking for more time. Everything after followed from this.17 Aug
STRIKETuesday–Wednesday: two Iranian missiles land off the UAE; a strait vessel struck, one casualty; Trump denies Kushner's "active conversations". The theatre widened to Gulf-state waters and the diplomatic track was publicly cut down by its own side within a day.18–19 Aug
SHIPPINGThursday: three China-linked supertankers turn back; UAE moves toward sanctions; transits hold near −19.5%. The strait's closure became physical for every flag, and the neighbourhood began picking the American side of the squeeze.20 Aug
POLITICSFriday: Washington vows its toughest sanctions and asks China — Beijing refuses; Iran and Oman quietly resume Hormuz talks. The economic escalation launched without its key enforcer, while the only de-escalation channel of the week opened in Muscat. Both facts are live into Monday.21 Aug

Oil ended the week at 86.86 WTI (+5.4%) with Brent's $93 handle intact, gasoline reached the US voter, and gold's record run said the hedgers expect neither loop to break. The regime consequence is direct: CPI y/y at 3.3 against the 2.5 floor stays propped open by energy, keeping Policy tightening alive into its sixth week. The single scenario that unwinds all of it — a Muscat framework — went from nonexistent to embryonic on Friday.

Unpinned, into Jackson Hole and Nvidia

GAMMAMonday opens the first negative-gamma tape of the run — net −$2.2B, spot below the 7,680 flip. Dealers amplify instead of dampen from here: wider ranges, live stops, trends that carry. Both BAC stops sit 2–4% away on a tape that just got faster — no position needs adding, every level needs respecting.Mon 24 Aug
FEDJackson Hole symposium — Powell speaks with $93 Brent against a cracking consumer. The rate path has to choose which problem it fears more. A hawkish lean lands on an unpinned tape; a dovish one feeds the gold trade. Either way it is the macro event of the week.late week
EARNINGSNvidia reports — the AI audit's verdict from the one desk that sees all the order books. After a week of chips −10%, Intel below its offer price, and tepid OpenAI numbers, guidance here either arrests the de-rating or accelerates it. Aldemar's INTC is a direct passenger.next week
LEVELSThe levels that decide the book. BAC: stops 60.39 (Gabriel) and 59.65 (Aldemar) below, 62 overhead — reclaim it and Thursday's break reads as expiry noise. INTC: the 89.75 week low against the 81.10 stop, with 95 the trapped-longs line overhead. GOOG: 340 reclaimed, watch the fresh gamma map Monday.Mon 24 Aug

Two positions sit in planned drawdowns with stops standing, one sits in profit, and the realized column already holds a clean −1R. Nothing about next week asks for a decision before the levels do — the work is letting a faster tape come to them.
